title: Usage Signal Investigator & Smart Escalation Orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We get frequent noise and low-signal alerts on usage/cost/latency dashboards. On-call and SREs spend significant time triaging each alert to determine blast radius, likely root cause, and next steps. This ticket builds an automated "Usage Signal Investigator" service that enriches detected anomalies across the data pipeline (ingest → metrics store → billing) and an orchestration layer that chooses escalation actions (suppress, auto-comment, page, create incident) based on confidence and impact policies.

Goals:
- Correlate anomalies across token-usage, request-latency, and billing spikes within a rolling 60m window and attribute to likely cause (model rollout, infra region, quota spike, client SDK change).
- Enrich alerts with contextual evidence: top-5 affected routes, model_id, customer_tenant examples, recent deploys, related GitHub PRs, relevant console traces and sampling of raw request payloads (sanitized).
- Implement confidence scoring and policy-driven escalation: low-confidence -> ticket to triage queue; medium -> notify Slack channel with auto-suggested runbook steps; high -> create PagerDuty incident and attach next-step checklist.
- Reduce false positives by 40% and mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) by 30% in the first month of rollout.

Scope: backend orchestration and investigator enrichment logic only. UI work (alert detail page) will be a follow-up ticket. This ties into existing anomaly detectors and the usage signal pipeline but introduces a deduplication and cross-signal correlation layer upstream of alert dispatch.

Non-goals: building new anomaly detectors, replacing existing SLO definitions, or changing billing calculations.
acceptance_criteria: Investigator service subscribes to anomaly topic in Kafka and produces enriched alert messages to 'enriched-alerts' topic with schema version v1
For every incoming anomaly, investigator attaches at least three contextual artifacts (top routes, last deploy hash, example tenant IDs) within 30s of detection in 95% of cases
Policy engine makes deterministic escalation decision and logs rationale; a policy dry-run mode is available before any paging is enabled
Automated suppression reduces duplicate alerts (same root cause fingerprint) by >=40% compared to baseline week
Playbook suggestions include a one-click link to affected Grafana dashboard and the relevant runbook in the ops runbook repo
tasks: Design event schema for enriched alerts and document in console-analytics/docs/enriched-alert-schema.md
Implement correlation worker: sliding-window coalescing, similarity fingerprinting, and root-cause heuristics
Build policy engine with configurable rules stored in Console config service and feature-flagged rollout
Add quick enrichment adapters: Deploys (CI API), Routes (metrics DB query), Billing spikes (billing snapshot), Example payload sampler (redaction + storage)
Integrate with notification bridges: Slack channel hooks, PagerDuty API, and internal triage queue service
Create telemetry: metrics for enrichment latency, false-suppression rate, and decisions logged to BigQuery for evaluation
End-to-end test harness + canary: replay historical anomalies and measure suppression/precision/recall
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use streaming correlation (Flink-style) over batch backfills to keep MTTA low; tradeoff is more stateful workers to manage and increased infra complexity

Confidence scoring will combine heuristic signals (fingerprint match, correlated metric deltas) and a lightweight ML model trained offline. Decision: initial rollout uses heuristics only, ML model planned for Q2 to avoid training data bias early
Store enriched alert payloads in encrypted S3 with retention 90 days to balance forensic needs and storage cost
Keep public-facing alert formats minimal and keep detailed enrichment in internal-only channels to avoid leaking customer data
